persons.note: A CONTEMPORARY CHICAGO PAPER OF 1833-1835 PRINTS THIS PERSON BY NAME IN THE TOWN. Read from death_notice, newspaper_1833_1835, newspaper_letter_list. THE GRADE IS THE OWNER'S RATIFIED LADDER OF 2026-09-03 (G1b), applied to every identity at once by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py and spent onto this card by tools/mint_civic_residents.py; the evidence blocks below carry the reading AS READ, its locator and the record it came from, so the page can be gone back to. WHAT IS RECONSTRUCTED: everything except the person and the sources — no dwelling, no trade, no origin, no family, no party. A BOUND FROM THE RECORD, NOT AN ARRIVAL. newspaper_1833_1835 names this person at Chicago by 4 February 1834 and nothing says when they came. The bound is at or before the scene date, so the person was at Chicago by 1 July 1835 on this record's own evidence. No figure is drawn (L1).

merge_ruling.for_merge: One letter in the stem of a twelve-letter Dutch surname, 'Henry' identical, and the Vanderbogart card is documented as a man: Fergus's old-settler notices print 'Bogart, Dr. Henry Van der' and 'Van der Bogart, Dr. Henry' with a death of 8 April 1835, and the Democrat sets 'H. Van Den Bogart' on 4 February 1834 and 'H. Vanderbogart' on 20 May 1835. 'Vanderbogert' is set four times in the corpus and nowhere outside this town's own records. The town holds exactly one of each.
merge_ruling.against_merge: THE PARTICLE IS ALREADY RULED AND THE STEM IS NOT. T-0842's C7 merge in the `vanderbogart` cluster folded Van Den against Van der on the printer's own practice, read at the Democrat of 4 February 1834 — that is the PARTICLE. What separates these two cards is a vowel inside the stem, a against e, and no printing reached is caught setting both: 'Vanderbogert, Henry' is the 1833 tax list and nothing else, and no issue, roll or notice carries the two spellings together. C7's demonstration does not transfer from the particle to the stem — that is C9's question and C9's page is missing. D7.

age_band.note: THE BAND THIS PERSON'S OWN BIRTH YEAR PUTS THEM IN on 1 July 1835. It is a view of a value already on this card and adds nothing to it; it exists so the age axis can be read across the whole layer at once, beside the bands the model draws for everybody else.

sex_basis.note: A FORENAME THAT STANDS IN ONE SEX'S NAMING ONLY. 'Henry' is read as male because 1 person in this layer whose sex a source records bears it (lampman_henry_s), and it stands in the yankee male forename pool of this town's own attested naming. Nothing about this person is recorded; the name is the whole of the reasoning, and the table that licenses it — data/research/residents/forename_sex.json — refuses a name its own evidence splits, refuses Jean, Marion, Leslie and Francis by name, and refuses an initial outright.

birth_year.note: A BIRTH INTERVAL OUT OF A DEATH NOTICE, NOT A RECORD OF A BIRTH. The page prints the death as 'April 8, 1835' and the age as 'aged 25'. An age of 25 completed years means at least 25 and less than 26, so the birth falls between 1809-04-09 and 1810-04-08: the birth year is 1809 or 1810. The subtraction is this project's; the page states no year of birth. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints the entry "Van der Bogart, Dr. Henry, died, Naperville, Ill., April 8, 1835, aged 25.", and its header admits the list also names citizens who arrived after 1843 and others merely prominently connected with Illinois history — so a match here is never evidence of residence in 1835 and never moves a grade. The match to this person was adjudicated in data/research/old_settlers/death_notices_crosswalk_1835.json and written onto this card by tools/spend_old_settlers.py; this pass only spends its arithmetic into a birth year. Both sides of the match spell a forename out — the crosswalk's thin matches, where a single initial is the whole of the discriminator, are refused rather than spent.

research_note: MINTED FROM THE CONSOLIDATED CIVIC, CHURCH, PRESS, BOOK AND CENSUS EVIDENCE (T-0513, T-0514). THE HOUSEHOLD IS A CONTAINER, NOT AN ARGUMENT: every other record here is written unattested in its own block, because the lists that name this person name a person and not a family. What is claimed is that the sources cited on the member below name them at Chicago, and the grade is the owner's ratified ladder applied by tools/consolidate_resident_evidence.py --build and spent by tools/mint_civic_residents.py, which prints every refusal. docs/LIBERTIES.md L215 carries the liberty and the tension with L213.

old_settler_deaths.note: LATER EVIDENCE OF A DEATH, BESIDE THE 1835 CLAIMS AND NOT INSIDE THEM. Fergus's 1843 directory (1896) prints an obituary list of old settlers, and one of its entries meets somebody of this name. THE HEADER OF THE LIST IS QUOTED ABOVE, and it is the limit the whole reading turns on. It does not mean the person was in Chicago in 1835, and it does not mean they arrived before 1843 — the list's own header, quoted above, says it also names citizens who arrived later and others merely 'prominently connected with Illinois history'. A match means one thing: a name in the 1835 layer and a name in this list agree on surname and first initial, and the list gives that name a death date and an age. The date and the interval are the payload. Whatever is carried is carried as evidence of a DEATH and of an interval the birth falls in, never as an 1835 fact and never as a grade. T-0513 consolidates and T-0514/T-0515 apply; this file changes no record. This pass WRITES THE EVIDENCE AND MOVES NO GRADE. A death notice printed in 1896 says a person of this name died on a day; under the ratified ladder (T-0513) that is later evidence about a DEATH, and it is never an 1835 residence. T-0515 applies the ladder against every source at once; this pass hands it the evidence and not the verdict.
